description: We’re a student hackathon team passionate about AI, software development, data science, and space technology
summary:
Space Explorer is a free 3D browser game that lets kids aged 7–12 play as junior astronauts on Mars and the Moon. Instead of just reading about space, players walk around a colony, drive a rover and fix equipment like oxygen, water and power systems through 40 story missions (20 on each world).

The challenge: space education is often too abstract for children, and they rarely see the trade-offs behind real missions. In our game, every choice has a cost. Saving power today can mean less air tomorrow. Each mission ends with a short recap in plain language that explains the science and why it matters.

Real NASA data keeps it honest. Radiation risks are tied to NASA's DONKI space-weather feed. Every data source in the game is clearly labelled Live, Archived or Sample. If NASA's service is slow, the game switches to saved data automatically.

It runs in any browser with no download or account, so it works in classrooms and at home. Events change between plays, so failing teaches kids instead of punishing them. The goal is simple: make real space science playable, trustworthy and a fun first step toward STEM.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Space Explorer is a 3D adventure game that runs in the web browser. A child becomes a junior astronaut and chooses one of two worlds: Mars or the Moon. Each world has 20 story missions in 4 chapters. Players walk around a colony, drive a rover, and repair equipment such as oxygen, water, power and communication systems. Each repair is a small hands-on puzzle, like matching wires, turning a valve, aligning a dish or balancing temperature. After each mission, the child gets stars, badges and a short recap. The recap explains the science idea in plain words and adds a fun fact.

HOW IT WORKS

1. A mentor character (Commander Nova on Mars, Commander Vance on the Moon) gives a briefing.

2. A golden trail, a compass bar and a minimap guide the player to the target.

3. The player walks or drives there and presses E to use the equipment.

4. A puzzle or mini-game appears, and solving it earns points and a badge.

5. A recap teaches the science behind what the child just did.

Progress for each world is saved in the browser, so kids can stop and continue later.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Many children find space science abstract, because it is taught through textbooks and videos. This game lets them practise it. They see why a base needs air, water and power, why radiation shelters matter, and how gravity differs on the Moon (1.62 m/s²) and Mars (3.72 m/s²). Our goal is to make real space science free and playable, and to give kids a fun first step toward STEM. It also works as a short classroom activity for teachers.

REAL NASA DATA

The game uses real NASA data, and it always labels where each piece comes from:

- Live: NASA DONKI solar-flare data and NASA OSDR space-biology studies, fetched while the child plays.

- Archived: real stored measurements, such as radiation readings from the Curiosity rover and Mars terrain data.

- Sample: backup data used if NASA's service is slow or offline. The game switches to it automatically after about 3 seconds, so it never breaks.

This helps children and teachers tell what is real and what is simulated.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

- React 19 and TypeScript for the menus, HUD and mini-games

- Three.js for all 3D worlds, rovers, buildings, characters and maps

- Vite for building the project

- NASA DONKI and OSDR public APIs for the science data

- Netlify for free public hosting, with no login needed

- GitHub for version control and open code

There are no paid services and no servers or databases. The game runs entirely in the browser, with no download or account.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

- Two full worlds in one project, each with its own gravity, terrain, crew and story.

- Almost nothing is loaded from image or 3D model files. Terrain, planets, astronauts, rovers and buildings are all generated by code, which keeps the game small and fast to load.
